These probabilities are priors from how MLP training usually behaves. I didn't run any code or look up the benchmark tables.

- **Learning rate dominates.** At the high end (0.278 and 1), Adam training tends to diverge. At the low end (1e-5 and 3.59e-5), 243 epochs may not be enough to fit. So learning-rate edits change sign depending on the band, and their interactions with depth, width and batch size (more steps, more stability) are the most likely to be real.
- **Alpha only matters in the high band** (0.0167 and up). Low and mid alpha values are close to zero penalty, so most alpha conditions should give N. The exception is alpha moving up within the high band, which should clearly hurt.
- **Width gains shrink as width grows**, so moving width up helps less in the high band.
- **Batch size and learning rate are coupled.** Larger batches mean fewer updates, which makes a higher learning rate more useful. Smaller batches give many updates, so raising batch size from the low band costs little.
